FED.note: Merged from the research map plus two adversarial audits. Both auditors verified the dissent ledger against FOMC statements and both found the same load-bearing error: Logan, Kashkari and Hammack did NOT dissent for a hike in April 2026 - they supported the hold and objected only to the easing bias; only July 2026 is a hike dissent (9-3), and June 2026 was unanimous 12-0. That correction is applied throughout. The research committee note's claim that George's June-2022 dissent was the cycle's only dissent is false (Bullard dissented in March 2022 for 50bp) and is dropped. George's duplicated 'duplicate-guard' period is removed. Flat multi-year periods that both auditors showed were contradicted by roll calls have been split (Daly, Goolsbee, Hammack, Kashkari, Bowman, Waller, Harker, Mester, Collins, Powell). Speakers whose stance rests on emphasis rather than any separating vote (Jefferson, Cook, Barr, Kugler, Quarles, Bowman pre-2024, Warsh) are kept but demoted to low confidence per the UNSUPPORTED rule. Anna Paulson is ADDED (both auditors flagged her omission; she is a confirmed 2026 voter and Reuters places her DOVISH) - she is not on the supplied roster, so drop the key if the backtest roster rejects it.

Powell.why: Chair; no dissent in the whole window and sat between the poles in every regime (hawkish of Brainard/Evans in 2021, dovish of Bullard/Mester in 2022-23, between Miran and Schmid in 2025). Median by construction and by revealed behaviour.

Both auditors: the chair-defines-the-median rule expires when Warsh was sworn in 22 May 2026. As an ordinary governor there is no vote-based evidence either way, so 0 is a placeholder, not a measurement.

Bowman.why: Auditor A flagged UNSUPPORTED: no dissent, in the majority at both contested 2022 meetings, and the research's own 2021 hawkish tail is Waller/Quarles not her. Lean retained at low confidence.
Sept-2024 dissent preferring 25bp to the committee's 50bp - the first Board dissent in roughly 20 years, and the most cut-resistant voter of that phase.
July-2025 dissent FOR a cut alongside Waller - the first double governor dissent since 1993. A genuine crossing to the dovish pole.

Auditor B, from the roll calls: she voted WITH the majority to hold at both Jan-2026 (Miran and Waller dissenting for cuts) and Apr-2026 (Miran sole dissenter). Still dovish, but not the pole of Warsh's committee.

Williams.why: Both auditors CONFIRMED: votes at every meeting, zero dissents across the entire window, present in the voting-for roster at every contested meeting. Maximal-exposure zero-dissent record - the strongest basis for a structural 0.

Waller.why: Auditor B: the 2021 taper pole was Kaplan/Rosengren from spring and Bullard from June; Waller's 'early this fall' call is August, so hawkish of the Board median but not the extreme.
The Board's hawkish tail through the hiking cycle, backing the 75bp increments ahead of Cook, Jefferson and Barr.
Nov-2023 'something appears to be giving' pivot; argued 50bp in Sept 2024; dissented FOR a cut in July 2025 with Bowman and again in Jan 2026. Reuters 22 Jan 2026 places him in the top DOVE bucket.
Dropped the dissent in March 2026 and rejoined the majority; sits between the Bowman/Paulson cut camp and the Logan/Kashkari/Hammack hike camp.

Jefferson.why: Auditor A's thin-record objection extends here: four years of always-voting membership, no dissent, no separating vote. Dovish-leaning centrist lean retained, confidence demoted.

Collins.why: Neutral from arrival; voted for all three 2025 cuts without dissenting while Schmid and later Goolsbee did.
Auditor A: the research's own rationale concedes a late-2025 hawkish drift (supporting a pause) that the flat 0 never registered. She is not a 2026 voter, so this rests on speeches alone.

Logan.why: Persistent hawkish extreme; uneasy about the 50bp Sept-2024 cut, and dissented for a 25bp HIKE in July 2026 (9-3) with Hammack and Kashkari. Correction accepted from both auditors: the April-2026 dissent was against including an easing bias while SUPPORTING the hold, not a vote for a hike.

Barkin.why: Career centrist, never dissented including as a 2021 and 2024 voter; frames policy as balancing both mandates rather than taking a side.

Kugler.why: UNSUPPORTED (auditor A): never dissented, voted with the majority at every decisive meeting of her tenure, and was absent from the July-2025 meeting where a dovish lean could have been shown. Lean retained at low confidence.

Cook.why: Same shape as Jefferson: reliable vote for the 2022-23 hikes, never argued for a higher terminal rate, easing-friendly in 2024-26 - but no dissent and no separating vote, so low confidence.

Schmid.why: Both auditors CONFIRMED precisely: voted FOR the Sept-2025 cut, then dissented against the Oct-2025 and Dec-2025 cuts preferring no change. The mirror image of Miran and the hawkish anchor of the 2025 cutting debate.

Musalem.why: Repeatedly argued inflation risks skewed to the upside and urged caution on the pace of easing, but voted for all three 2025 cuts without dissenting - a notch below the Schmid/Logan/Hammack tail.

Harker.why: Auditor A: the research documented a mover and then averaged him to 0. In 2021 he was among the earlier voices for tapering 'sooner rather than later', hawkish of Brainard/Evans/Kashkari. He also appears in the March and June 2022 voting rosters as Boston's alternate.
The other half of the same shift: among the earlier voices for slowing hikes and then cutting, dovish of Bowman/Logan/Mester. Never dissented, hence low confidence.

Barr.why: UNSUPPORTED (auditor A): a regulatory specialist with no dissent in four years of always-voting membership; he did not join Bowman and Waller when they dissented for a cut in July 2025. Association-based lean retained at low confidence.

Kashkari.why: The committee's best-known dove in the taper debate and the polar opposite of Kaplan, Rosengren and Bullard.

The most dramatic flip in the sample - by the June-2022 SEP he carried one of the most hawkish dots and argued through 2023 for further hikes. (SEP dots are anonymous, so the 'single most hawkish dot' superlative is not verifiable.)
Supported the 2024-25 easing in principle, more open to cuts than Schmid/Logan/Hammack but never in the Goolsbee/Daly/Miran camp.
Both auditors: he voted WITH the majority to hold in Jan and Mar 2026, and Reuters 22 Jan 2026 puts him in HAWKISH, a bucket below the HAWK heading. +2 from January back-projects three months.
First formal break in Apr-2026 (dissent against the easing bias while supporting the hold), then the July-2026 dissent for a 25bp hike with Logan and Hammack.

Daly.why: Dovish pole of the taper debate with Brainard, Evans and Kashkari against the Kaplan/Rosengren/Bullard push.

Both auditors reject the flat -2: no dissent in 5.5 years, voted for every 2022-23 hike including the 75bp moves and for the Sept and Dec 2024 cuts. Reuters 22 Jan 2026 places her one notch INSIDE the DOVE bucket that holds Waller and Miran.

Bostic.why: One of the earliest hawks of the cycle: flagged a possible 2022 hike in Jan 2021 and backed a faster taper plus one or two 2022 hikes in Nov 2021.
Crossed to the dovish side of a uniformly hawkish committee - first to float a September pause (May 2022) and the leading 'one more hike then stop' voice through 2023.
Auditor B CONFIRMED, and notes Reuters actually puts him in the top HAWK bucket in Jan 2026; held at +1 because he never dissented and was not a 2026 voter. Retired 28 Feb 2026.

Hammack.why: Auditor A, from the roll call: her first FOMC vote was FOR the 50bp Sept-2024 cut that Bowman dissented against - 'hawkish from her first months' is refuted.
Dec-2024 dissent preferring to hold, sustained caution through 2025, and the July-2026 dissent for a 25bp hike. April-2026 was a dissent against the easing bias, not a hike vote.

Mester.why: Auditor A: her 2021 taper record is undifferentiated from Bostic's, so the flat +2 back-projects. Early-taper advocate, hawkish of the median.

Loudest advocate of front-loaded 75bp moves and a higher terminal rate. Confidence held at medium because she never dissented - she was in the majority at both the March and June 2022 dissent meetings.

Goolsbee.why: The committee's leading dove and author of the 'golden path' while Bullard, Mester, Logan and Bowman still wanted tightening.

Auditor A: he voted for the Sept and Oct 2025 cuts sitting in the majority flanked by Miran (50bp) and Schmid (none) - not pole behaviour. A -2 to +1 jump inside one month is a step function fitted to one event.
Dec-2025 dissent AGAINST the cut with Schmid, preferring no change; Reuters 22 Jan 2026 then classes him HAWKISH. Both auditors CONFIRMED; the research's hedge is unnecessary.

Miran.why: The best-evidenced entry in the whole set, confirmed by both auditors against all six statements: dissented at every meeting he attended - 50bp in Sept/Oct/Dec 2025 and for a 25bp cut in Jan/Mar/Apr 2026.

Warsh.why: Both auditors: UNSUPPORTED. He did not join the Hammack/Kashkari/Logan hike dissents and characterised the hold as having large majority support, but the affirmative evidence (dropped guidance, June dots penciling a hike) runs hawkish. 0 is a placeholder on three meetings of evidence. Note: the claim that the new statement stopped publishing the vote split is FALSE - July 2026 was 9-3 with dissenters named.

Brainard.why: The Board's dovish pole through the taper debate and the internal counterweight to Waller and Quarles.
Turned rhetorically hawkish in early 2022 and voted for the 75bp moves, but was the leading voice for slowing the pace and respecting policy lags.

Clarida.why: Anchored the 'transitory' centre with Powell and Williams - dovish of Kaplan/Rosengren/Bullard/Waller on tapering, hawkish of Brainard/Evans/Kashkari in flagging a 2022 liftoff.

Quarles.why: UNSUPPORTED (auditor A): a supervision vice chair with a thin rate-policy record, no dissent, and 2021 produced no dissents at all. The whole case is one mid-2021 taper remark. Lean retained at low confidence.

George.why: Both auditors CONFIRMED, including the reasoning: a reputational hawk whose only in-window dissent (June 2022, preferring 50bp to 75bp) ran in the DOVISH direction on pace, which correctly places her behind Bullard and Mester. The research's duplicate 'duplicate-guard' period has been deleted.

Evans.why: Career dove and architect of outcome-based/average-inflation-targeting thinking; the most persistent voice for patience as a 2021 voter.

Bullard.why: Still in the 'too early to talk about tapering' camp in early 2021 - not yet the outlier he became.

The most hawkish participant of the tightening cycle; DISSENTED in March 2022 for 50bp - the cycle's opening dissent, verified by both auditors and fatal to the research note's claim that George's was the cycle's only dissent.

Rosengren.why: One of the two loudest early-taper voices of 2021 with Kaplan; called publicly for a September taper announcement. Resigned 30 Sept 2021.

Kaplan.why: The earliest explicit hawk of the period - taper 'sooner rather than later' from spring 2021 and a 2022 hike dot when almost the whole committee was at zero through 2023.

Paulson.why: ADDED - not on the supplied roster, but both auditors flag the omission as breaking the 2026 dovish end. Confirmed 2026 voting member (Jan-2026 and Apr-2026 roll calls) and Reuters 22 Jan 2026 places her DOVISH on labour-market weakness. Low confidence: no dissent, short record.

ECB.note: The ECB publishes no votes and no attributed positions, so this is a communication-and-scorecard ordering, not a voting ledger. Only four members have any attributable dissent evidence in the whole window (Holzmann x3, plus the Dec-2021 PEPP objection attributed to the Belgian, Austrian and German governors, plus Visco's March-2023 public rebuke) - those entries carry high confidence and nothing else should. Both auditors independently verified the Econostream live table (9 Aug 2026) and found the research's transcriptions clean, so no sign is reversed. Both auditors also found the SAME roster hole: seven sitting members omitted, four of them above the median, which made the visible council read ~0.10 more dovish than the real one. Kaasik, Radev, Zigman, Dolenc, Patsalides, Santos Pereira and Demarco are therefore ADDED (all off the supplied roster - drop them if the backtest roster rejects the keys). Bucket rule applied consistently: Econostream >=1.25 -> +2, 0.5-1.0 -> +1, 0.25 -> 0, -0.25 to -0.75 -> -1, <=-1.25 -> -2. The committee note's claim that 'in every case the successor is less extreme than the predecessor' is FALSE on the map's own numbers (Villeroy -1 to Moulin -2, Guindos 0 to Vujcic +1, Muller +1 to Kaasik +2, Scicluna 0 to Demarco -1) and is dropped. Mauderer is NOT a Governing Council member (Bundesbank Vice-President, Nagel's alternate) and is zeroed.

Lagarde.why: Anchored the 'transitory' consensus; Econostream -0.5 in Feb 2022 against a council average near -0.05.
Once she led the 50bp and 75bp hikes she occupied the centre she was constructing; Econostream now scores her 0.25, exactly the committee median.

Nagel.why: Succeeded Weidmann and joined the top hawk tier - 'several more rate hikes' plus faster balance-sheet run-off.
Endorsed the easing cycle and avoided Weidmann's vanguard role; Econostream 0.75, level with Wunsch, Kocher and Vujcic and a clear step below Schnabel and Kazimir.

Guindos.why: Both auditors: UNSUPPORTED. The argument is entirely negative ('no scorecard placed him on either wing'), which supports 'unresolved' rather than 'median', and no scorecard placement exists for any sub-period. 0 retained as the least-wrong integer.

Lane.why: Both auditors CONFIRMED: Econostream scored him -1.75 in Feb 2022 against a council average near -0.05 - effectively the floor alongside Panetta. Caveat: some of a chief economist's measured dovishness is institutional, since tabling the staff proposal is the job.
Drift to the centre as author of the hiking and then cutting proposals; Econostream -0.75 against a 0.25 median, a full notch above Panetta, Rehn and the -1.25 cluster.

Schnabel.why: In 2021 she defended PEPP flexibility and was explicitly not read as a German hawk; near the council median.

Both auditors reject the claim of continuous primacy from Nov 2021: the Econostream ranking of 18 Nov 2021 names Weidmann, Knot and Holzmann at the hawkish end, not her, and she spent 2022 authoring and defending the consensus rather than pushing beyond the 75bp delivered. Hawkish of the median, not its head.
Econostream 1.5, alone at the top of all 27, and by mid-2026 arguing further hiking would be needed while Rehn, Cipollone, Moulin and Stournaras were on the dovish wing.

Villeroy.why: Both auditors show the one piece of split-related evidence is inverted - Knot and Holzmann were pressing to WIND DOWN PEPP, not to preserve its flexibility (Austria is among the three Dec-2021 objectors). 0 may survive as a genuine early normaliser ahead of Lane, but the stated basis is gone, so confidence is low. (Auditor B argued for -1.)

Among the earliest and loudest advocates of cutting - 'maximum optionality', pushback on cutting only once a quarter, door open to a larger December move. Grouped with Centeno and Stournaras as particularly dovish.

Knot.why: Placed at the hawkish extreme with Weidmann and Holzmann in Econostream's Nov-2021 ranking; repeatedly floated further 75bp moves and early QT through 2022-23.
Econostream's July-2023 update was headlined 'Knot Ranked Notably Less Hawkish'; by Oct 2024 he was warning about undershoots as much as overshoots. Still above the median but out of the top tier.

Panetta.why: Both auditors CONFIRMED at both ends of the window: Econostream -2.0 (explicit floor) in Feb 2022 and -1.75 (lowest of all 27) on the live table in Aug 2026. The Board-to-governor seat change in Nov 2023 did not move him.

Rehn.why: On the dovish wing of the PEPP period with Lagarde, Cos and Centeno, notably softer than the other northern governors.
Backed frontloading and a rapid move to neutral, which was the council consensus - the median position, not a hawkish one.

Auditor B CONFIRMED against the live table: Econostream -1.5, second-lowest of 27, strictly below Stournaras, Cipollone and Moulin. Auditor A objected that the 'his 2026 hawkish remarks reflect the council-wide shift' clause is unfalsifiable; the named ranking is the harder evidence and wins.

Makhlouf.why: A centrist who tracked the consensus through the hiking cycle and by spring 2023 was suggesting hikes were near their limit.

Econostream 0.5, a quarter-point above the 0.25 median. Auditor A argues the integer map promotes him spuriously into the 0.75 cluster; auditor B keeps him at +1. Disagreement unresolved, so the stance is kept and the confidence demoted.

Cipollone.why: Took Panetta's Board seat and his position; the council's most persistent undershoot-warner with a dated, distinct, repeated public record. Auditor A explicitly declined to challenge this entry as the best-evidenced of the -1.25 cluster.

Elderson.why: Both auditors agree the -1 was a placeholder: the research itself says it is 'inferred from Board alignment rather than distinct statements'. He has never been reported on either side of any split, and his one measured data point (Econostream 0.25) is exactly the median.
Econostream 0.25, exactly the committee median, level with Lagarde, Escriva and Simkus.

Stournaras.why: A fixed dovish point on every scorecard - resisted the pace of hikes in 2022-23, asked 'why not cut at every meeting?' in 2024. Auditor A correctly notes Econostream has him at -1.25, i.e. THIRD among national governors behind Panetta (-1.75) and Rehn (-1.5), so the 'most vocal dove among governors' superlative is false and confidence drops to medium; auditor B keeps him in the -2 bucket, which the mapping rule supports.

Mauderer.why: Both auditors: category error. She is Bundesbank Vice-President and Nagel's ALTERNATE, not a Governing Council member, and does not appear on the 27-name Econostream table. Zeroed so she carries no signal; the honest action is deletion.

Centeno.why: Consistently among the three or four most dovish members - pressed for 'a clear message of gentler rate hikes' in 2022-23 and warned about undershooting from 2024.

Wunsch.why: Econostream dated his formal entry into hawkish territory to November 2021; through 2021 he pushed the exit debate with Kazimir and Vasle.

Auditor A's dating fix applied: the December-2021 PEPP objection - fxstreet's sourcing names the Belgian, Austrian and German governors - falls one month INSIDE the old +1 period, so the step to +2 starts in Dec 2021. One of only four members in the window with attributable dissent evidence.
Econostream 0.75, level with Nagel, Kocher and Vujcic - still hawkish of the median but off the extreme.

Cos.why: A consensus technocrat routinely grouped with the doves in accounts of the 2022-23 divide while being distinctly less dovish than any of them; never a wing voice.

Sleijpen.why: Econostream 0.5, a quarter-point above the median. Auditor A argues for 0 (he explicitly refuses the hawk/dove label, non-committal line, barely a year of votes); auditor B keeps +1. Stance kept, confidence low.

Visco.why: Both auditors CONFIRMED: his March-2023 public rebuke of colleagues for pre-committing to further hikes is the most explicit open expression of a Council split by anyone other than Holzmann - self-attributed, dated and directional.

Delgado.why: Both auditors: UNSUPPORTED. Three-month acting caretaker between Cos and Escriva with no distinguishing intervention and no scorecard placement. 0 is the right default but it means 'unresolved', not 'centrist'.

Kazimir.why: UNSUPPORTED (auditor A): the one dissent-type fact offered is false - the Dec-2021 objectors were the Belgian, Austrian and German governors; Slovakia is not among them, and the research states that same three-country set twice elsewhere. Lean retained at low confidence on the exit-debate record only.
A 'keep powering through' hawk who never left that end; Econostream 1.25 in 2026, second only to Schnabel.

Holzmann.why: Both auditors CONFIRMED - the only entry in the whole ECB set a voting-and-dissent lens can validate: July-2021 guidance reservations ('a step too far'), sole dissenter on the June-2024 first cut, dissent again June 2025, plus the Dec-2021 PEPP objection attributed to the Austrian governor.

Moulin.why: Both auditors flag UNSUPPORTED - weeks in post, no observed record, and Econostream at two months is pricing a seat rather than a person. The rank survives (-1.25, bottom five of 27, tied with Stournaras and Cipollone), so the bucket is kept and the confidence is low.

Weidmann.why: Both auditors CONFIRMED: named at the hawkish extreme with Knot and Holzmann in Econostream's Nov-2021 ranking, and the German governor is one of the three named Dec-2021 objectors - a genuine reported dissent, not an inference from tone.

Kazaks.why: Notably less hawkish than his Baltic peers in the PEPP period, sitting near the council centre.

The loudest frontloading advocate of 2022 - 50bp for July, 75bp 'appropriate' for October, and warning through Sept 2023 against betting on H1-2024 cuts. Confidence demoted: auditor A argues that advocating exactly the decision delivered is the median under the map's own rule, and he never appears in the reported December-2022 75bp minority.
Moderated to the 'gradual, meeting by meeting' camp, warranting caution on further cuts alongside Muller.
Completed the traverse: Econostream -0.25, below the 0.25 median and below Simkus, Escriva and Elderson.

Muller.why: A quiet hawk above the Lagarde/Villeroy centre through the PEPP debate.

Auditor B, from the research's own cited source: the Econostream article of 4 Feb 2022 scores Muller at 1.25 (raised from 1.0) on a day when the council average was -0.07 - the same number Kazimir carries today at +2. The flat +1 is refuted for the hiking cycle.
A firm hiker who warned against rushing cuts in June 2024, sitting above the median with Vasle, Simkus and Reinesch but below the top tier.

Vasle.why: In the 2021 exit-debate group with Wunsch and Kazimir, a firm hiker through 2022-23, and pushing back on bets on bigger cuts in Oct 2024 - consistently a notch above the median, never in the top tier.

Simkus.why: Grouped with the Baltic hawks - as late as June 2023 saying 'at least one more rate hike is required'.
Drifted to the middle during the easing cycle; Econostream 0.25, exactly the median.

Vujcic.why: Ranked on the hawkish side from Croatia's entry; Econostream 0.75, level with Nagel, Wunsch and Kocher.

Auditor A: the move from a rotating Group-2 governorship to the always-voting Vice-Presidency is one of the two largest changes in actual influence in the dataset, and the map cannot both say the Vice-Presidency erases a personal line (Guindos) and preserves one (Vujcic). Stance carried forward at low confidence.

Herodotou.why: Both auditors: UNSUPPORTED, a pure nationality-bloc inference with no dissent, no reported minority and no scorecard placement in three-plus years. The prior is undercut by his successor Patsalides landing at exactly the median (0.25). Both suggested 0, so the correction is taken.

Scicluna.why: Ranked among the doves in Econostream's table through 2021, above Lane/Panetta/Visco/Stournaras and well below the northern hawks.

Econostream's March-2022 headline says only that he was 'no longer ranked among the doves', which is a boundary crossing rather than a placement at the median, and his final years were dominated by a domestic legal case. UNSUPPORTED (auditor A, who argued for -1); stance kept, confidence low.

Reinesch.why: Econostream 1.0, fourth-equal of 27. The auditors split: A says UNSUPPORTED and would zero him (speaks on monetary policy very rarely, no dissent, not among the Dec-2021 objectors, and citing the scorecard as evidence for a rounding of the scorecard is circular); B says the 1.0 belongs in the +2 bucket with Radev. Researcher's +1 kept as the midpoint, confidence low.

Kocher.why: Took Holzmann's seat but not his position: Econostream 0.75, a full step below Schnabel, Kazimir and Reinesch, where Holzmann had been the top hawk and the only serial dissenter.

Escriva.why: Ranked squarely at the median despite the Spanish seat's dovish reputation - Econostream 0.25, level with Lagarde, Elderson and Simkus.

Kaasik.why: ADDED - both auditors flag the omission. Econostream 1.25 on the live table, joint-SECOND most hawkish of all 27 behind only Schnabel, above Reinesch, Radev, Nagel, Wunsch, Kocher and Vujcic. Took Muller's Estonian seat.

Radev.why: ADDED - Bulgarian National Bank governor, seated on Bulgaria's January-2026 euro entry, which the research note announces and then never rosters. Econostream 1.0, tied with Reinesch and bucketed identically.

Zigman.why: ADDED - took the Croatian governorship Vujcic vacated for the Vice-Presidency on 1 June 2026. Econostream 0.75, the same score as Nagel, Wunsch, Kocher and Vujcic.

Dolenc.why: ADDED - filled the Slovenian seat the research itself flags as vacant after Vasle. Econostream 0.75. Start date approximate.

Patsalides.why: ADDED - succeeded Herodotou at the Central Bank of Cyprus in April 2024. Econostream 0.25, exactly the council median; the research even says so inside Herodotou's rationale without creating the entry.

Santos Pereira.why: ADDED - succeeded Centeno at the Banco de Portugal. Econostream -0.25, dovish of the median, the same score this map gives Kazaks at -1.

Demarco.why: ADDED - succeeded Scicluna at the Central Bank of Malta. Econostream -0.75, tied with Lane and firmly on the dovish side of the median.

BOE.note: The only committee in this set with a fully attributed vote for every member at every meeting, and both auditors independently re-verified the load-bearing votes (Sep-2025 QT: Pill GBP100bn / majority GBP70bn / Mann GBP62bn; Nov-2025 5-4 hold; Dec-2025 5-4 cut; Feb-2026 5-4 hold; the 2026 hike escalation Pill alone in April, +Greene in June, +Mann in July). Two repeated fabrications are removed: there was NO casting vote at Sep-2023 (a 5-4 on a nine-member committee cannot tie), and Nov-2025 was a 5-4 HOLD with Bailey on the hold side, not a hold dissent he declined to join. The 2021 block has been rebuilt: Bank Rate was unanimous at every 2021 meeting and the only dissents all year were on the gilt stock, so the dovish gradations both auditors called pure rhetoric-ranking are removed - Saunders and Haskel go to 0 (both auditors agreed, and both members' own next votes contradict the dovish label), while Vlieghe keeps the dove pole on a published, dated argument for delay. Several period starts that back-projected a later dissent are corrected (Pill, Taylor, Breeden, Greene). The 2026 caveat both auditors flag: since Feb-2026 there has been NO dovish dissent (Mar-2026 unanimous, then 8-1, 7-2, 6-3 hawkish), so Dhingra and Taylor remain the relative doves but the pole is no longer expressed in dissent.

Bailey.why: Both auditors CONFIRMED the score: no dissent in any of the 45 decisions, and in the majority at every split checked name-by-name. The stated evidence is corrected - there was no Sep-2023 casting vote (5-4 on nine members), and in a 5-4 every member of the five is equally pivotal, so the 0 is a default from 45 non-dissents rather than positional evidence.

Mann.why: Hawkish on the balance sheet before rates: voted with Ramsden and Saunders in Nov-2021 to cut the gilt target to GBP855bn while still voting to hold Bank Rate.

The most persistent hawk on the committee for three years - 50bp Feb/May/Jun 2022, 75bp Sep-2022, alone for 75bp in Dec-2022, hike dissents through Feb-2024, and SOLE dissenter against the Nov-2024 cut.

Both auditors reject -1. The window contains two meetings and only the first is dovish: she voted 50bp with Dhingra in Feb-2025, then in Mar-2025 Dhingra was the SOLE cut dissenter, meaning Mann voted to hold. She framed the 50bp as front-loading toward a higher-for-longer path, not easing.

Auditor B, on ordering plus a named ranking: Mann is strictly hawkish of Lombardelli (+1) on every divided vote in the period (May-2025 hold vs Lombardelli's cut; Jul-2026 hike vs Lombardelli's hold), which forces +2 on this scale, and MUFG's Jul-2026 member sentiment scoring ranks her top of the committee at 80 (Pill 71, Greene 65). Auditor A argued for +1 on her GBP62bn QT preference and her being last of the three to break for a hike; that nuance survives inside the +2.

Pill.why: A median voter for his first twenty meetings with not one dissent; 'Table Mountain rather than Matterhorn' described the majority's reaction function rather than a position to the right of it.
Auditor A: his first dissent of his entire MPC career is Aug-2024. Jan-Jun 2024 he voted with the majority at every meeting, identically to Bailey and Broadbent, so the +1 started seven months early.
Voted against the Aug-2024 cut with Mann, Haskel and Greene; the most cut-resistant internal member, but still short of Mann, who dissented alone against the Nov-2024 cut when he voted for it.

Both auditors call this the best-evidenced score on the map: May-2025 hold dissent with Mann; the only GBP100bn QT vote in Sep-2025 against a GBP70bn majority; dissents against the Aug and Dec 2025 cuts; and the SOLE hike vote at Apr-2026 (8-1), two meetings before Greene and three before Mann.

Greene.why: A hawkish dissenter from the start but a step behind the lead hawks - she took the 25bp majority line at her first meeting when Mann and Haskel wanted 50bp, and dropped the hike call in Feb-2024 while they maintained it.

Both auditors: +2 from January is scored with future information. In May-2025 Greene voted FOR the 25bp cut with Bailey while Mann and Pill voted to HOLD - she was dovish of both hawks in the very window she was scored two notches above Mann. Feb-2025 she took the 25bp majority line, Sep-2025 she was in the GBP70bn QT majority.

Those placements are zeroed or demoted. Mendes is moved to -2 from Oct-2025 on auditor B's argument that the map awarded +2 three times and -2 only once, ending Jun-2022 - four years with a named hawk pole and no dove pole; his Oct-2025 'reacting to temporary movements could cause more volatility' is the explicit mirror of Kozicki's Oslo restraint case. Alexopoulos (from Mar-2025) and Gosselin (from May-2026) are off-roster, so the 2025-26 cross-sections are structurally incomplete.

Under the consensus model the Governor owns the final call and the communique is his, so he is the anchor the deputies are measured against - and his record is genuinely two-sided (the 100bp Jul-2022 hike, but also the dovish 50bp Oct-2022 surprise against a 75bp consensus, the first G7 pause in Jan-2023, and two 50bp cuts in late 2024).

Auditor A flags it as day-after-decision boilerplate restating the 7 Sept 2022 statement, so confidence is demoted. The personally differentiated evidence really begins with Nov-2023 'get used to higher interest rates'.

Auditor A flags UNSUPPORTED: it is inference from silence plus a portfolio action.

Both auditors: UNSUPPORTED. His BoC profile shows no speech at all between Sep-2024 and Nov-2025 - a 0 from silence, sitting exactly at the hinge of the claimed hawk-to-dove reversal.

SNB.note: The smallest and least transparent committee here: a three-member Governing Board that has NEVER published a vote, dissent, minute or attributed view, and the new 'Summary of discussion' (from Sept 2025) is deliberately collective - both auditors fetched it and confirmed it contains no 'one member'/'some members' language. Every placement is portfolio plus speech emphasis. Both auditors independently flagged the same two structural problems: PORTFOLIO DETERMINISM (Dept II -> hawk, Dept III -> dove, Dept I -> house line, so each score transfers to whoever next occupies the chair) and QUOTE SELECTION (the current formula 'negative rates are available if price stability requires it, but the bar is high' is spoken by ALL three sitting members, and the map deals each of them a different half of it). Confidence is therefore low almost everywhere. RE-CENTRING (see notes): the researcher's Maechler 0 for 2022-08 onward left the three-member board at Jordan 0 / Schlegel +1 / Maechler 0 - one-signed - so Maechler is moved to -1 for that stretch; Moser is set to -1 for Jul-2023 to Sep-2024, the only other stretch that came out one-signed, on the strength of his running Department III ad interim; and Schlegel is split at his Oct-2024 accession to the chairmanship, taking auditor A's period boundary with auditor B's magnitude. 'Steiner' is Barbara Janom Steiner, President of the Bank COUNCIL (the supervisory body), with no monetary-policy role - scored 0 so the key resolves without inventing a policymaker. Antoine Martin (Vice-Chairman from Oct 2024, hawkish end with Schlegel) is off-roster, so the post-2024 voting board is only partly scored here.

He retired six weeks after the first hike without revealing a preference on the pace.

Jordan.why: Auditor B CONFIRMED: in a three-person collegial board with no published votes the Chairman's line IS the committee line, and Swiss reporting describes Jordan as the dominant force in the Directorate since 2012. He personally owned both poles of the cycle (-0.75% with unlimited intervention, the surprise 50bp Jun-2022 hike ahead of the ECB, the flip to selling FX, the first G10 cut in Mar-2024). Auditor A flags UNSUPPORTED because the score is an identifying normalisation that no conduct could falsify - hence low confidence and the label: this is an anchor, not a measurement.

Maechler.why: Auditor A CONFIRMED - the only SNB entry built on dated, first-person, on-point quotes: 'not anywhere close' to changing policy (Jun-2021) and 'our expansionary monetary policy is absolutely necessary', from the Dept III holder who co-authored the Nov-2020 negative-rate steering blueprint, at the exact moment Zurbruegg was warning that mortgage vulnerabilities were high. Auditor B argued for -2 as the dove pole; -1 kept because ±1 already spans both signs on this three-person board. End date moved from 2022-05 to 2022-07 per auditor A: every cause of her repositioning postdates it (Zurbruegg retired 31 Jul 2022, Schlegel arrived 1 Aug, her convergence quotes are Sept/Oct 2022).
